aggressive_definition_excerpt: There was heterogeneity in the association between docosapentaenoic acid and prostate cancer by grade of disease (P = .006); the association was statistically significant for low-grade disease but not high-grade disease.
study_design: Individual participant data meta-analysis of seven prospective studies using conditional logistic regression on prostate cancer cases and controls.
reason: The abstract reports total incident prostate cancer associations and an analysis by grade that includes high-grade disease. It gives 5,098 cases and 6,649 controls but does not explicitly state a total analytic participant N, which was not inferred by addition. No high-grade case count is reported.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was, respectively, 14% and 16% greater in the highest fifth of eicosapentaenoic acid (20:5n-3) (OR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.01 to 1.29, Ptrend = .001) and docosapentaenoic acid (22:5n-3) (OR = 1.16, 95% CI = 1.02 to 1.33, P trend = .003), but in each case there was heterogeneity between studies (P = .022 and P < .001, respectively).
estimate_classifications.reason: The eicosapentaenoic acid estimate is for prostate cancer risk overall. The abstract does not identify this numeric estimate as high-grade or another aggressive endpoint.
